history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE PAIR: seq 1149 'Belur Math' (id belur-math-howrah) is the same institution — keep-or-merge decision needed. FLAG: the CSV town is wrong - Belur Math is NOT in Durgapur. It is the international headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission in Belur, Howrah district, West Bengal, on the west bank of the Hooghly river; town field corrected to Belur. Founded by Swami Vivekananda (chief disciple of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa); the 40-acre campus land was purchased 4 March 1897 and holy relics of Sri Ramakrishna were installed 9 December 1898. The main Sri Ramakrishna Temple was consecrated 14 January 1938, built with munificence of two American ladies (Helen Rubel and Anna Worcester). The architecture fuses Hindu, Buddhist and Christian motifs as a symbol of the unity of religions. The campus also houses temples of Swami Vivekananda, the Holy Mother Sri Sarada Devi and Swami Brahmananda, the Samadhi Enclosure, and the Ramakrishna Museum. Belur Math railway station (2003) serves the campus.

name: Belur Math Temple
town_description: Belur is a town in the Howrah district of West Bengal on the west bank of the Hooghly river, famous as the seat of Belur Math, the international headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission. Directly across the river from Dakshineswar, it is connected by road, rail (Belur Math station) and Hooghly ferries, and draws pilgrims and visitors daily, especially for festivals and the evening aarti.
